target.title: fix(acp): exec approvals target the matching concurrent prompt
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ACP clients could lose the real exec approval title and tool-call correlation metadata, causing concurrent prompts that share one Gateway session to miss or misroute a permission request.

An explicit but unmatched `toolCallId` could also degrade to session-only routing and associate an authorization prompt with an ACP interaction that did not own that tool call.

Related: #3257  
Follows: #79337

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix connects one canonical metadata path from the public `exec` caller through the closed Gateway request schema, pending approval record, WebSocket broadcast, ACP parser, and `session/request_permission` request.

ACP correlation now treats a present `toolCallId` as authoritative: it relays only a unique pending match within the same session. The legacy unique-session fallback remains only for events that omit the identifier. Duplicate and explicit-mismatch cases fail closed.

The repair also:

- keeps `title` and `toolCallId` optional across the Gateway protocol and generated Swift model;
- uses the existing approval-title sanitizer and exec display resolver;
- shares approval metadata and correlation helpers so the oversized production files satisfy the repository LOC ratchet;
- fixes the approval-request regression test to call the exported host registration function.

Approval decisions, command hydration, allowed options, provider behavior, and unrelated channel delivery are unchanged.

## User Impact

ACP clients can show the intended exec approval title and attach the permission request to the originating tool call. Concurrent prompts sharing a session no longer lose a uniquely correlated approval, and contradictory explicit identifiers are not silently routed to another prompt.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Public exec calls preserve their display title and tool-call identifier through `exec.approval.requested`; ACP routes a matching identifier to the correct pending prompt and rejects an explicit mismatch instead of broadening the authorization match.

**Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 24.15.0, current head `b056cc2f21842cdd49ac7028fa5e6ca5b9db66ab`, isolated OpenClaw state/config, a real loopback Gateway, separate authenticated operator and exec-tool connections. The earlier full-boundary capture used a live Gateway, configured model, production ACP stdio bridge, and official ACP SDK client at `59985b5f0da9f3c3fc131cf71459169e83ad2c26`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
PATH=<Node 24.15.0>/bin:$PATH \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts \
  src/agents/bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts
```

The current-head scenario starts the real Gateway, connects a separate approval operator, invokes the public exec tool with `toolCallId=exec-approval-e2e`, observes `exec.approval.requested`, resolves allow-once, and waits for command completion.

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
Current-head Gateway E2E
  HEAD: b056cc2f21842cdd49ac7028fa5e6ca5b9db66ab
  approval event toolCallId: exec-approval-e2e
  approval title: contains "smoke"
  selected decision: allow-once
  command exitCode: 0
  command output: smoke

Full Gateway + official ACP SDK concurrent capture
  HEAD: 59985b5f0da9f3c3fc131cf71459169e83ad2c26
  shared sessionKey: agent:main:acp-concurrent-proof-96719488-817e-4369-89e3-27e79e0c1ca1
  permission sessionId: a873a0ea-970a-45d6-908c-31d0d13c5a76
  permission toolCallId: call_0d0229bba971421f80ead9f8
  permission title: print text · `printf ACP_CONCURRENT_FIRST_e0b1abab-8663-4ddb-b818-c94e52e4b9dc`
  selected option: allow-once
  command exitCode: 0
  command output: ACP_CONCURRENT_FIRST_e0b1abab-8663-4ddb-b818-c94e52e4b9dc
```

**Observed result after fix:** The current-head real Gateway run broadcast the originating tool-call metadata and completed the approved command. The current-head ACP permission-relay suite passed all 15 cases, including unique concurrent matching, absent-ID compatibility fallback, duplicate ambiguity, and explicit mismatch rejection.

**What was not tested:** The live-model + official ACP SDK capture was not repeated on the current head; freshness is supplied by the current-head real Gateway E2E plus the current-head ACP correlation suite. No third-party ACP GUI, Discord account flow, macOS, Windows, iOS, or Android client behavior is claimed.

### Current-head verification

```text
ACP translator permission relay: 15 passed
Exec approval request suite: 13 passed
Gateway approval metadata handlers: 2 passed
Gateway-hosted exec approval E2E: 1 passed
Core test typecheck: exit 0
Changed-surface lint: exit 0
TypeScript LOC ratchet: checked 12 changed production files
Changed-surface format check: passed
Protocol + generated Swift outputs: stable
git diff --check: exit 0
```

### Review findings addressed

- Explicit unmatched `toolCallId` values now fail closed; session-only fallback applies only when the identifier is absent.
- Added a current-head real Gateway E2E run and reran the full current-head ACP permission-relay suite.
- Applied the recommended authoritative-identifier policy while preserving the legacy absent-ID compatibility path.
- **CI:** Fixed the undefined host-registration test call, made core test types pass, and reduced all oversized changed production files to satisfy `check:loc`. The prior full lint/deadcode failures pointed to unrelated files not changed by this PR; the new head CI will re-evaluate them against the current base.

### Risk and scope

This remains a security-boundary change because it controls which ACP interaction receives an exec approval. The fail-closed rule narrows routing when identifiers contradict each other; it does not broaden execution permissions. Optional protocol fields remain backward-compatible, titles use the existing sanitizer, and events without identifiers preserve the previous unique-session fallback.
